column1: # Offline-resolver overrides:  <term as printed>  TAB  <target the index resolves>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and why it is not aliases_src/{lang}_curated.tsv
# Those files are inputs to the BUNDLE BUILD (indicator/fhir/embeddings/
# lexicon.py). Their right-hand side is a descriptive English phrase —
# "Total cholesterol TC", "Leukocyte count WBC" — which is exactly the shape
# This file serves the OFFLINE RESOLVER at runtime, where the right-hand side
# has a different job: it must itself be a key the finished alias index can
# look up. "Total cholesterol TC" is a fine build input and a dead end at
# lookup time. Rewriting the build inputs to suit the resolver would have
# quietly degraded the semantic pipeline, so the two concerns get two files.
# Every row here was a documented failure in test_engine_coverage.py. Two
# kinds of failure appear, and the second is the dangerous one:
#   MISS  — "LDL cholesterol" resolved to nothing. The index is built from
#           LOINC long common names, so it knows the formal name and the lab
#           short code (LDL-C) but not the phrase humans write. Plain English
#   WRONG — "血红蛋白" resolved to Hemoglobin A1c: a different test, returned
#           with full confidence. It matches 301 index rows and the commonness
#           prior likes HbA1c best. A resolution-rate metric scores this as a
#           success; a patient reading the report would not.
# CONTRIBUTING: this is the lowest-barrier useful PR in the repo. Find a term
# that resolves wrong or not at all, add one row here plus one case in
# mirobody/test_engine_coverage.py, and raise COVERAGE_FLOOR. Any language.
# Targets are validated by the test suite, so a typo'd target fails CI rather
# The bare plural nouns (Leukocytes, Erythrocytes, Hematocrit) are not index
# keys on their own; the LOINC short names are. "HCT" alone is not usable as
# a target either — it collides with Calcitonin.

column1: # 日本語 was the weakest language in the 154-term hunt (13 of 20 missed): the
# katakana forms and the short kanji names a 健康診断 prints are absent from the
# machine-derived ja.tsv, which carries LOINC's formal translations.
# NOTE: 血圧 / "blood pressure" on its own is deliberately absent. It names a
# panel, not one observation, and the index answers it with the diastolic code
# — a confident wrong answer. An honest `unresolved` is the better output.
# Target `!unresolved` means: never answer this term. These name a PANEL or a
# category, not one observation, so any single code is a wrong answer. Measured
# before blocking: "blood pressure" matched 183 index rows and the commonness
# prior returned 8462-4 — the DIASTOLIC code — so a systolic reading filed
# under it lands in the wrong series. Callers must ask which measurement is
# meant. (Terms that legitimately map to a panel/set code are NOT listed here:
# 血压 → 18684-1 "Blood pressure Set" is a panel code for a panel term.)
# Specimen-prefixed Chinese, which is how a real report prints them. The index
# carries the bare noun (肌酐, 尿酸, 总胆固醇) because that is the alias shape
# the lexicon was built from; a printed 中文 panel writes 血清肌酐 / 尿白细胞.
# Two of these did not merely miss — they resolved CONFIDENTLY WRONG, which is
# the failure mode this project scores as worse than silence:
#   血清肌酐  -> 44760-7 MELD score          (its long name contains "serum creatinine")
#   血清白蛋白 -> chicken serum albumin nGal d 5  (an allergen panel entry)
# Found by resolving the terms printed in mirobody/test_engine_coverage.py's
# newest cases, which were lifted verbatim off a 2025 physical report.
# CBC full names as a 中文 report prints them; the ABBREVIATION already
# resolved (MCV -> 30428-7), the spelled-out Chinese did not. Same shape as the
# 血清 rows above, found in the same 9-page scanned report.
# Fourth sweep, prompted by the platform API docs: `POST /v1/data` says device
# and wearable data is the MAIN form structured records take, and every example
# in it names indicators the way a device SDK does — `steps`,
# `resting_heart_rate`, `sleep_duration`. The lab panels above were covered;
# this vocabulary was not. Underscore flattening (engine.py `_candidate_keys`)
# handles the snake_case shape, so these rows only need the human wording.
# Two were WRONG rather than missing:
#   SpO2  -> a Deprecated "Fractional oxyhemoglobin ... Preductal" row with no
#            LOINC at all — resolved=True carrying an empty code.
#   HRV   -> 40991-2 Rhinovirus+Enterovirus RNA. NOT fixed here: HRV is a real
#            abbreviation for human rhinovirus as well as heart rate
#            variability, so the right answer is a decision, not a lookup. The
# Fasting glucose is its OWN LOINC concept (1558-6, COMPONENT
# `Glucose^post CFst`), not plain glucose (2339-0). These rows used to target
# `Glucose`, which collapsed a fasting reading into the generic glucose
# series — the distinction the ordering physician made, thrown away on

column1: # The short codes a CBC / 生化 printout puts in its own column. They were the
# worst-covered surface in the resolver, and two of them were WRONG rather than
# missing — the same near-miss class as 血红蛋白 -> HbA1c, just wearing the
#   HGB -> 4548-4  Hemoglobin A1c        (a diabetes marker for a CBC line)
#   HCT -> 1992-7  Calcitonin            (a thyroid hormone for hematocrit)
# Targets are the phrasings the index actually keys on; each row was checked
# with `mirobody resolve` before being written down.
# Abbreviations that name more than one test resolve to the WIDESPREAD
# reading rather than refusing. A panel name is a different case and stays
# blocked (see the non-answers section): there, no single observation code
# can be right. Here one reading dominates ordinary use by a wide margin,
# and an honest miss on `CA` helps nobody when 钙 is what a 生化 panel means
# by it ~always. What must not happen is the index picking for us — that is
# how HGB became HbA1c — so each is written down.
#   CA = 钙 (calcium), not 癌抗原 CA-125/CA19-9 (those spell themselves out)
#   PT = 凝血酶原时间 (prothrombin time), not 前列腺素 / 甲状旁腺
#   MG = 镁 (magnesium), not the unit mg
#   Cr = 肌酐 (creatinine), not chromium — and note `Cr`/`CR` casefold to one
#        key, so only one row can win
# ══ 日本語 — 健康診断 terms the ja.tsv sweep does not carry ═══════════════════
# ja.tsv is 16,809 rows but its right-hand side is overwhelmingly SNOMED-shaped:
# diseases and organisms (Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus, Ornithine
# transcarbamoylase deficiency), not LOINC observations — only 3% of its
# distinct targets are keys the observation index can look up. Everyday 健康診断
# names come out at 20/24 all the same, via zh/ja_curated plus the index; these
# four are what a spot-check of the panel found missing.
# HRV is heart rate variability. It is also the abbreviation for human
# rhinovirus, and the index preferred that reading: `HRV` answered 40991-2
# Rhinovirus+Enterovirus RNA, a PCR panel, for what every wearable on the
# market means by those three letters. Same rule as CA/PT/MG above — the
# widespread reading, written down rather than left to the commonness prior.
# 凝血酶原时间 answered 34714-6 INR: a DERIVED ratio, not the time itself.
# 血圧 is 血压 in Japanese and had no entry at all, so it missed — while the
# Chinese form answers 18684-1 "Blood pressure Set". The overrides header states
# the rule those two were breaking: a panel TERM mapping to a panel CODE is a
# correct answer and is not blocked (which is why 血压 is not in the
# non-answers section). One language getting the panel code and another getting
# silence is not a policy, it is a gap — surfaced by the eval harness, which
# asked why the two behaved differently.
# Half of what a report prints is not a number, and half the shipped corpus is
# not Qn — 25,156 Ord rows, 7,859 Nom, 4,258 SemiQn. A urinalysis panel, a
# serology screen and a blood type are all 阴性/阳性/++ results, and the ones
# below simply had no entry at all.
# Targets are the [Presence] / [Type] variants, because that is what these
# tests ARE. `resolve_reading` then moves along the scale axis when a value
# says otherwise, so a term that also has a quantitative form (乙肝表面抗体 is
# reported both as a titre and as reactive/non-reactive) still lands right.

column2: Hemoglobin [Presence] in Urine by Test strip
